summary.claim_boundary: Sixteen-seed, four-radius prospective confirmation testing whether the higher finite-step retraction cost of moving-fibre natural gradient vanishes as a discretization effect while its restricted action ordering converges. Six algorithms are generated causally in a transported eight-dimensional chart projected into the current response kernel at every step, with a common 20% capability endpoint. No fitted lambda or scalar composite is used. A pass prospectively confirms the restricted six-algorithm Moving-Fibre F16 scaling result in this frozen CNN--MNIST model; it is not complete-kernel optimization, continuum geometry, local stationarity, GPT-2 transfer, global variation, or a universal learning law.
